segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל שֶׁבָּא בְּחַמִּין מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — שׁוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּחַמִּין בְּשַׁבָּת. וְכׇל שֶׁלֹּא בָּא בְּחַמִּין מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — מְדִיחִין אוֹתוֹ בְּחַמִּין בַּשַּׁבָּת, חוּץ מִן הַמָּלִיחַ הַיָּשָׁן וְדָגִים מְלוּחִין קְטַנִּים וְקוֹלְיָיס הָאִיסְפְּנִין, שֶׁהַדָּחָתָן זוֹ הִיא גְּמַר מְלַאכְתָּן.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «Any» salted food item «that was» already «placed in hot water,» i.e., cooked, «before Shabbat, one may soak it in hot water» even «on Shabbat. And anything that was not placed in hot water before Shabbat, one may rinse it in hot water on Shabbat» but may not soak it, «with the exception of old salted» fish «and small salted fish and» the «kolyas ha’ispanin» fish, «for which rinsing» with hot water «itself is completion of the prohibited labor» of cooking.

moves.summary: What was cooked before Shabbat may be soaked in hot water on Shabbat

moves.cueHe: וכל שלא בא בחמין מערב שבת
moves.summary: Uncooked items may be rinsed, except old salted fish and kolyas ha'ispanin whose rinsing completes their cooking

positions.claim: rinsing salted fish and kolyas ha'ispanin completes their cooking and is prohibited
